1-phytaes are naturally occurring enzymes that are involved in the dephosphorylation of phytate, a major phosphate storage compound and signaling molecule in plants, 1-phyatase activity is required and sufficient for XopH-dependent Bs7-mediated immunity, and Xanthomonas infection results in a Xanthomonas- and XopH-dependent phytate dephosphorylating reaction in planta.

(1) The T3E Xanthomonas XopH possesses 1-phyatse activity that is required to trigger Bs7-mediated immunity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular and cellular mechanisms that underlie the interaction between plant pathogens and their plant hosts.
the molecular mechanisms of plant-pathogen interactions.
the elucidation of the molecular basis of plant-microbe interactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
XopH is a 1-phytosiderophore synthase, which is required for Xanthomonas virulence, and that it can be recognized by plants carrying the Bs2 or Bs7 resistance gene.
XopH possesses 1-phyatase activity that is involved in Bs7-triggered immunity.
the T3E XOPH possesses 1-phytoside hydrolase activity that degrades InsP6 to the defense related InsP5.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
XopH interferes with plant signaling by dephosphorylating InsP6 at position 1.
the T3E Xanthomonas effector XopH interferes with plant phosphate signaling by converting InsP6 to the signaling molecule InsP5.
XopH is a naturally occurring 3-phytase (myo-inostitol-hexakis-phosphate phosphohydrolase) that dephosphorilates myo-inositol hexakisphosphate (InsP6) at the C1 position.
The main takeaway from our work is that
XopH is the first T3E that has been shown to interfere with a plant hormone pathway by enzymatic action.
XopH represents a new class of T3E that targets the plant hormone signaling network.
